differences.title: 1. RENDERING STRATEGY
differences.leftDesc: App Router leverages React Server Components (RSC) to render components on the server by default, reducing client-side JavaScript bundle size and improving initial load performance.
differences.rightDesc: Pages Router primarily relies on client-side rendering after initial server-side rendering (SSR) or static site generation (SSG), often leading to larger JavaScript payloads for interactivity.

differences.title: 2. DATA FETCHING
differences.leftDesc: RSC allows direct async data fetching within components on the server, eliminating the need for separate data fetching hooks or libraries on the client for initial renders.
differences.rightDesc: Pages Router typically uses `getServerSideProps`, `getStaticProps`, or client-side `fetch` calls, requiring explicit data fetching logic in specific page files or components.

differences.title: 3. LAYOUTS
differences.leftDesc: App Router introduces intuitive `layout.js` files for creating shared UI and nested layouts that preserve state and avoid re-renders across navigation.
differences.rightDesc: Pages Router implements shared layouts using higher-order components or wrapping pages, which can be less ergonomic and may lead to re-renders on navigation.

differences.title: 4. ROUTING ARCHITECTURE
differences.leftDesc: App Router uses a convention-based routing system within the `app` directory, mapping folder structures directly to URL paths, enabling features like route groups.
differences.rightDesc: Pages Router uses a strict file-based routing system within the `pages` directory, where file names and paths directly dictate routes, offering simplicity for straightforward applications.

differences.title: 5. STREAMING
differences.leftDesc: App Router seamlessly supports streaming HTML from the server to the client, allowing parts of the UI to render progressively while data is still being fetched.
differences.rightDesc: Pages Router requires manual implementation using libraries or specific SSR patterns to achieve HTML streaming, adding complexity to the development process.

differences.title: 6. SERVER ACTIONS
differences.leftDesc: App Router natively supports Server Actions, allowing direct execution of server-side mutations and form submissions from components without explicit API route handlers.
differences.rightDesc: Pages Router necessitates creating separate API routes (e.g., `/pages/api`) to handle server-side data mutations and form submissions, creating a distinct separation.

differences.title: 7. CODE ARCHIVING
differences.leftDesc: App Router encourages colocation of UI components, server logic, and even tests within feature-based directories, improving maintainability and developer experience for complex features.
differences.rightDesc: Pages Router enforces separation, with pages in `pages` and API routes in `pages/api`, which can lead to scattered logic and harder navigation for related functionalities.
